reran:
I ran everything from a copy in the scratchpad, so no repo files changed. The machine load average was 5–18 because other agents were running.

**Part A subset**
- What ran: `a/run-a.mjs --runs 3 --only css,motion,gsap,autoanimate`. That covers css plus its three View Transition variants, motion and motion-hw, gsap, and autoanimate.
- Bundle sizes and lines of code: all 8 identical, for example CSS 1.1 KB, GSAP 57.0 KB, Motion 27.7 KB.
- Interruption result: identical in all 17 cells.
  - The View Transition swallows input 3/3.
  - The css-vt-list-pe variant is continuous.
  - css-vtpe jumps to the old target 3/3, with a 24.4% jump. results.json has 25.6%, but the report text says 29.5%, which matches neither.
  - motion-hw sheet jumps to the old target.
  - AutoAnimate grid jumps 3/3 (100%). AutoAnimate list was continuous 3/3; the report had 4/5 continuous.
- Reduced-motion states (normal / out of the box / with guard): identical in every cell.
- Sheet movement while the main thread was blocked for 400 ms: CSS 224 px; Motion transform strings 194 px (report 224); Motion shorthands 0 px; GSAP 0 px.
- rAF at rest (callbacks per second): CSS 0, Motion 60.5 (59), GSAP 97 (103.5), AutoAnimate 0.
- Script time: CSS 6.5 ms (5.9), Motion 111 ms (181), GSAP 129.5 ms (146). The GSAP < Motion ordering did not reproduce.

**Motion repros**
- `repro-motion-transform`: 0.032 at 50 ms vs 0.969 with the shorthand; 56 px became 5.2 px after two frames. Matches the report.
- `repro-motion-reduce`: under reduce, whileTap had 0 intermediate frames, and 13 with `reduceMotion: false` (report 0 and 14). Matches.

**rAF probes**
- `rest-probes`: all 18 probes match. ScrollTrigger measured 77.5 and 74, anime.js onScroll 59.5, React Spring useScroll 57.5, Motion `scroll(scaleX)` 60, everything else 0.
- I also measured the loops at 12 s and 30 s: they are still running at 50–64/s.
- `rest-b`: all 7 variants match. Rive and main-thread dotLottie run 58–60 rAF/s while showing 1 distinct frame; `stopRendering()` / `freeze()` bring them to 0; lottie-web, CSS and the dotLottie Worker are at 0.
- WASM sizes recomputed with Node zlib level 9: Rive canvas 794.9 KiB, canvas-lite 356.3, dotLottie 487.4. Matches.

**Part C development fixtures** (`c/run-c.mjs`, held-out step skipped)
- Spec findings: 42 true positives, 1 false positive, 0 misses.
- The false positive: the GSAP page's 100 ms press read as "static: changed in one frame" at load 15–18. The CSS/WAAPI two-frame rescue does not cover JS-driven animation.
- Flags: 76/76. Entry verdicts: 35/36.

**Not rerun:** Part B time to first frame and cost; the motion-react, anime, spring and theatre Part A variants; the held-out runner.

**Extra checks I added**
- motion.mjs on the six Part A pages with the reduce guard forced on. This is a balanced set (moves 5, instant 18, fades 19). The reduced-motion outcome agreed with Part A 42/42.
- motion.mjs on five pages it was not developed on: `research/experiments/H-blind-eval/fixture/index.html` with my own 3-row spec, `a11y-lab/pages/flawed.html` and `fixed.html`, and `tools/regress/fixtures/a11y-wizard.html` and `govuk.html`. It raised 92 flags; 11 are clear false positives and about 7 more contradict motion.md §6.
- An 8-entry edge-case spec (invalid selector, missing target, a link that navigates, `key:Enter`, unknown tokens, hover interrupt, an entry with no id): no crashes.

problems.claim: Held-out check (the six Part A pages, never used for tuning ...): animates-or-not 42/42, reduced-motion outcome 42/42.
problems.problem:
The reference set has no negatives. In results.json, all 42 rows are 'moves' or 'fades' in the normal run (41 moves, 1 fades), and 41/42 are 'moves' under reduce-default. A checker that always answers 'animates / still moves' would score 42/42 and 41/42.

It was also used for tuning. The report's own history says the earlier misses (the @property counter, the React-mounted sheet, the wording for a counting number) were fixed in motion.mjs and in run-heldout's `redOf` mapping.

Pass/fail verdicts were not scored. `captures/c/heldout-css/motion.json` already fails correct rows: the scroll-driven reveal gets 'duration ~48–67ms outside medium', and the @property ticker gets 'text did not change'.
problems.fix: Drop 'never used for tuning'. Replace the check with the guarded pages (inject `window.__RM_GUARD=true`) compared against `single[*]['reduce-guard']`. That set is balanced, and I got 42/42 on it, which is real evidence for the reduced-motion classifier. Also score the pass/fail verdicts on those pages.

problems.claim: Flags 76/76 (precision 1.0); motion.mjs is ready as a Phase 5 gate / technical-qa.md checklist item.
problems.problem:
On five pages it was not tuned on, it raised 92 flags, with at least 11 clear false positives (about 88% precision):
- **hover-none on native form controls (8).** Flagged: `select` and `radio` in flawed.html (`#content select`, `#n1`, `#n2`); `#billing` and `#settings input` in fixed.html; `#street`, `#cor-town` and `#cor-country` in the wizard. The computed-style fingerprint cannot see the browser's native hover rendering.
- **GOV.UK back link.** Its hover changes `text-decoration-thickness`, which the fingerprint does not read.
- **GOV.UK header link.** Its hover adds `border-bottom: 3px solid`; the fingerprint has border colours but not widths or styles.
- **no-reduced-motion on a page with zero transitions or animations** (GOV.UK).

About 6 more flags contradict motion.md §6 ('Spinners and progress: keep'). Loading spinners are flagged `moves-under-reduce` (a warning) and `infinite ... off under reduce` (flawed.html, a11y-wizard, fixed.html).

It is also load-sensitive: the rerun failed the GSAP 100 ms press as static.
problems.fix:
- Skip native select, checkbox and radio in the hover check unless author CSS has a `:hover` rule for them.
- Add `text-decoration-thickness`, `text-underline-offset`, border width/style, and background-size/position to the fingerprint.
- Raise no-reduced-motion only when the inventory or the load motion is non-empty.
- Exempt small rotate-only loops and `role=progressbar` / `aria-busy` spinners from moves-under-reduce, or reword the flag to follow §6.
- Extend the two-frame rescue to JS-driven motion.
- Report precision on held-out pages, not only on the four fixtures.

problems.claim: Job→tool table: CSS transitions (@property for tickers); CSS scroll-driven reveals. Phase 5 gate: every motion.mjs row passes.
problems.problem:
On the correct, guarded CSS page, motion.mjs fails 3 of 7 rows, and each one is a technique the report itself recommends:
- **Scroll reveal.** The scroll-driven animation already exists before the trigger. `anims` keeps only animations first seen after the trigger, so `scrollLinked` stays false and a duration check is applied to a scroll-linked reveal.
- **Ticker.** It fails with 'text did not change', because `cvar` is only read while a transition is running.
- **View transition.** It reports 'the fade takes 400ms'. The 400 ms is the browser's own `::view-transition-group` animation; the fades are 150 ms.

Used as a gate, it would push builders away from the CSS techniques the same report recommends.
problems.fix:
- Detect scroll-linked timelines from the target's `getAnimations()` at trigger time.
- Accept a changing custom property or counter as satisfying `text`.
- Exclude `::view-transition-group` from the fade-duration check.
- Until these are fixed, report these cases as notes rather than failures.

problems.claim: CSS ticker via @property + counter() is enough (the 'CSS is enough' row, 1.9 KB for all seven).
problems.problem:
The lab's CSS ticker displays '01000' after 'To 1000'. The `<output>` keeps its static text '0' and `::after` appends the counter; I took a screenshot to confirm. The accessibility tree reads `status "1000": "0"`.

No measurement caught this, because the harness reads `--n`, not the visible text. More generally, `counter()` output is not in the DOM text: it cannot be selected, found or translated. It is also integer-only, with no locale grouping or decimals.
problems.fix:
- Fix the markup: empty the `<output>`, or set its textContent when the animation ends.
- In the job table, limit the @property counter to integer, decorative counts, with the real value in the DOM text.
- Otherwise, use a WAAPI or JS ticker that writes textContent.
- Re-check the ticker row with a visible-text assertion.

problems.claim: motion.mjs writes filmstrips (frames sampled at fixed times); attach them to the Phase 6 critique.
problems.problem:
Every filmstrip is clipped at 1280 px. All four `shots/c-*.jpg` are exactly 1280 wide: the 450 ms frame is cut and the 700 ms frame (the settled state) is missing. The cause: 8 cells of about 181 px, plus a 70 px label and padding, is roughly 1,520 px, rendered on a 1280 px default page.

For scroll rows, the crop is the top-left 900×600 of the viewport, so on the H-blind-eval page the cards being checked never appear in the strip.
problems.fix:
- Size the filmstrip page to its content with `setViewportSize`, or compute the scale from the available width.
- For scroll rows, crop to the target's rectangle after the scroll ends.

problems.claim: GSAP: a cubic-bezier needs CustomEase path syntax `M0,0 C0.2,0 0,1 1,1` [V: no cubic-bezier matches].
problems.problem: `CustomEase.create('out','0.2,0,0,1')` works: `setData` in CustomEase.js has an `l === 4` branch for exactly this. I evaluated both forms and they give identical values. Only the literal string `cubic-bezier(...)` fails.
problems.fix: Say that GSAP needs the CustomEase plugin, passing the four bezier numbers as `'0.2,0,0,1'`.

problems.claim: Spec `reduced: fade` = opacity/colour ≤ 200 ms (motion.mjs header; check message).
problems.problem:
There are three different numbers:
- motion.md §6 and §4 say a crossfade under reduce is ≤ 150 ms (`--dur-page: 150ms` under reduce).
- The motion.mjs header and its message say ≤ 200 ms.
- The code (line 810) fails only above 250 ms.

The report does not mention the conflict with the existing reference.
problems.fix: Use a single threshold taken from motion.md (150 ms plus a stated tolerance) in the code, the message, and the proposed spec wording.

problems.claim: motion.mjs handles setup errors and reports clearly (edge-case behaviour).
problems.problem:
No crashes, but several messages mislead:
- A `load` row whose target is missing or mistyped reports 'static: nothing changed', which reads as missing motion rather than a bad spec.
- An unknown easing token is ignored silently, while an unknown duration token is reported.
- A click that navigates away reports 'no data'.
- Hover rows still run with `--device phone`.
- The internal key '≈ __spec' leaks into the easing column.
- The under-reduce inventory counts the kill rule's 0.01 ms transitions as motion: 63 elements on the static fixture and 228 on a11y-lab `fixed.html`, more than the normal run.
problems.fix:
- Report 'target not found' when the target selector matches nothing.
- Report unknown easing tokens.
- Detect navigation and say so.
- Skip hover rows on phone and say so.
- Show the spec's easing name instead of '__spec'.
- Exclude transitions of 1 ms or less from the inventory.

problems.claim: Script time for the whole set: GSAP 146 < Motion vanilla 181 = anime.js 181 < Motion for React 209 < React Spring 398; React Spring rejected partly for 'highest script time'.
problems.problem: In my rerun Motion vanilla (111 ms) came in below GSAP (129.5 ms). Only 'CSS is far below any library' is stable. The View Transition jump is also misquoted: the report text says 29.5%, but results.json says 25.6% and my rerun got 24.4%.
problems.fix: Present script time as CSS vs libraries, not as a ranking. Drop script time as a reason to reject React Spring unless it is re-measured on a quiet machine with more runs. Correct the 29.5% figure.

problems.claim: Rive: avoid webgl2 unless measured on a real GPU. dotLottie: prefer the Worker version (main thread 20 ms/s instead of 255).
problems.problem:
The webgl2 advice comes from SwiftShader timings (first frame 1920 ms, 975 ms/s). The sound reason is its 897 KB of WASM, which does not depend on the GPU.

For the Worker, neither the worker's own CPU time nor whether it keeps rendering at rest was measured: '0 rAF/s' is main-thread only. Total CPU and battery use may not fall.
problems.fix: Base the webgl2 advice on its size. Label the Worker figure as main-thread only, and measure the worker's CPU, or state that it was not measured.

problems.claim: B: Native button + SVG/CSS 0.2 KB, 98 ms first frame vs Rive 409–957 KB, for 'an illustrated, stateful element'.
problems.problem:
The CSS/SVG row is a plain pill switch. It is compared against an illustrated Day/Night Rive scene and a Lottie toggle, so the cost of drawing an illustrated equivalent in SVG/CSS (the brief's mascot case) was never measured.

Its reduced-motion rule also moves the knob with `linear` easing, which contradicts motion.md §4 ('never linear for movement').
problems.fix: State that the CSS row is a plain control, not an illustration at the same level of detail. Keep the decision tree's control-first rule, but do not present 0.2 KB as the cost of an illustrated element. Change the knob's reduced-motion easing.

problems.claim: Rive canvas WASM 795 KB gz (new table) vs motion.md §8 'Rive (56 KB JS + 787 KB WASM)'.
problems.problem: Both numbers are correct but use different compressors. Node zlib level 9 gives 794.9 KiB; the gzip -9 command line gives 786.6 KiB. The report would add a second figure to the skill without explaining the difference.
problems.fix: Choose one method, state it, and update §8 consistently.

strongest:
These reproduced on rerun and are the ones worth putting into the skill:

- **View Transitions swallow input** for their whole duration: 3/3 on rerun. Clicks pass only with both `:root { view-transition-name: none }` and `::view-transition { pointer-events: none }`, and the next transition then jumps about 25%. This belongs in motion.md §5.
- **Motion's transform-string defects** reproduced exactly:
  - with no from-keyframe it starts at `scale(0)` (0.032 at 50 ms);
  - an interruption snaps to the old target (56 px to 5.2 px).
  - This correctly qualifies §7's advice to "animate the transform string".
- **Scroll features that never sleep:** GSAP ScrollTrigger (even when only registered), anime.js onScroll, React Spring useScroll and Motion `scroll()` with `scaleX` keep `requestAnimationFrame` at 57–77/s. At 30 s they are still at 50–64/s. Motion `scroll()` with a transform string, `scroll(callback)` and Motion for React `useScroll` sit at 0.
- **Rive and main-thread dotLottie at rest:** they keep rAF at about 58–60/s while showing 1 distinct frame. `stopRendering()` and `freeze()` bring it to 0; lottie-web and CSS stop by themselves.
- **CSS/WAAPI keep moving through a 400 ms main-thread block** (224 px); the Motion shorthands and GSAP move 0 px.
- **Motion for React under reduce:** `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` also removes whileTap press feedback, and `transition.reduceMotion: false` restores it. Confirmed in source (positionalKeys includes transforms) and by rerun.
- **GSAP licence facts:** no LICENSE file in the package, the "no charge" licence field, and the README's "100% FREE" wording. npm view confirms the field.
- **Sizes and lines of code** reproduce exactly.
- **Sample-asset licences:** rive-wasm, rive-react and dotlottie-web are MIT at the pinned commits.
- **The motion spec table and motion.mjs's trigger-and-sample core are sound.** The reduced-motion classifier agreed 42/42 with Part A on the balanced guarded set. On a page it had never seen (the H-blind-eval Milkline fixture) it found all 8 spec problems with no false positives: duration, easing, stagger, still moving under reduce, and missing press and hover.
- **Decision guidance keeps the skill CSS-first and control-first:** native control, then lottie-web light, dotLottie, and Rive only when there is a state machine or data binding. It does not push toward technology-first choices or game-development scope.
weakest:
- **Precision claims:**
  - The development-fixture 76/76 and 42/42 were tuned on those fixtures.
  - The "held-out" 42/42 has no negative cases and was also used for tuning.
  - On real held-out pages, flag precision is about 88% or lower.
- **The "CSS is enough for tickers" recommendation** rests on an implementation that shows "01000" and whose DOM text stays stale.
- **Using motion.mjs as a Phase 5 gate is premature.** It fails the skill's own preferred CSS scroll-driven reveal, the @property ticker, and a View Transition with a 150 ms fade.
- **Filmstrips** always drop the final frame.
- **Script-time ranking among the JS libraries** does not reproduce, and the 29.5% View Transition jump figure is not in results.json.
- **Rive webgl2 figures** are SwiftShader-only.
- **The dotLottie Worker "20 ms/s"** is main-thread only.
- **Search-snippet claims:**
  - Rive and LottieFiles pricing, and "publishing needs a paid plan since Oct 2025", come from search snippets.
  - The Figma Motion / `get_motion_context` path is untested.
- **The CustomEase "path syntax only" claim** is wrong.
- **Unexplained:** Theatre's 54 rAF/s in the full set.
- **Part B's CSS row** is a plain switch, not an illustrated element, so the "0.2 KB vs 409 KB" contrast overstates the case for the brief's mascot scenario.
